reconcile.connective: These expositors read Bethabara as the Jordan's own crossing-point, so John's 'beyond Jordan' town and the Synoptics' 'in Jordan' name one riverside site.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible poses the conflict directly: the Synoptics place the baptizing 'in Jordan,' John 1:28 sets it 'in Bethabara beyond Jordan.'

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible — "Where did John baptize?"
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013); skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/jordan.html

excerpts.excerpt_text: He was now baptizing in Jordan at Bethabara (Joh 1:28), the house of passage, where the children of Israel passed over …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly merges both location descriptions into one clause — 'baptizing in Jordan at Bethabara' — treating the Synoptic river and John's named site as the same place.

excerpts.excerpt_text: …the place here mentioned; which was a passage over Jordan, where much people walked to go on the other side, beyond Jordan; and where also John was baptizing …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Identifies Bethabara as itself 'a passage over Jordan' (a ford on the river) where John baptized, so the town-name and the river-name pick out one location.

pd_work.note: Gill treats John 1:28 directly, glossing Bethabara as a ford/crossing on the Jordan itself — the harmonizing reading surfaced on this row. (Checked against John Haley's Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), which does not treat this passage.)
